clue.text: Way of meeting online, mostly new — once divorcee goes out to bag fellow

indicators.note: to bag means to capture, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
goes out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged
mostly means the word loses its last letter, keeping most of it

parts.note: the word new itself, cut short

explanation.surface: A divorce story: a former spouse goes out on the town to pick up a man, while everyone else meets online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly new' gives NE; NE with ONCE and DIVORCEE is rearranged ('goes out') to VIDEOCONERENCE, which then bags F (fellow) to complete the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A video call linking several participants remotely is a modern method for holding a meeting over the internet.

clue.text: My servant works for church committee member

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked over, reshaped into something new

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their servant labours on behalf of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestryman is a parish lay official sitting on the vestry, the body running a church's secular business.

clue.text: Tory MP virtually led into taxi following party

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the party

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: into means the shortened word goes inside the taxi

parts.note: a minicab is a type of taxi booked by phone in Britain

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: led means ran, as in ran a company

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician is ushered into a cab after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually led' gives RA (RAN without its last letter), which goes into MINICAB; DO comes first. Dominic Raab is a British Conservative MP and former Foreign Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominic Raab is a Conservative member of the British parliament, so he is an example of a Tory politician.

clue.text: Top revealed belt

parts.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
a belt of land is a strip of it

explanation.surface: A shirt opens to show a belt beneath, or a tabloid exposes a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a garment, but it is the verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a rival is to surpass or exceed them, the same as to outstrip them.

clue.text: Sailor also called port in Japan

parts.note: OS is ordinary seaman, a common crossword sailor
AKA is the abbreviation for also known as

explanation.surface: A sailor, going by another name, turns up in a Japanese harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Osaka is a major Japanese city with a large commercial harbour on Osaka Bay.

clue.text: Releases colour, like a peach?

definitions.note: the answer is used here as an adjective describing a kind of fruit

parts.note: to release is to free, so releases gives frees
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Something lets its colour go, perhaps fading like a peach's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A freestone fruit, such as many peaches, has flesh that comes away cleanly from its stone.

clue.text: Think tank ultimately concerned with Conservative squeezing

parts.note: re is a word meaning regarding or concerning

indicators.note: squeezing means holding something tight inside
ultimately means take the final letter of tank

explanation.surface: A think tank, in the end, worries about the Tories crushing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to suppose or believe, so it is a synonym for thinking something is so.

clue.text: Flipping rubbish hotel that mostly is solvent

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rubbish something is to pan it, criticise it harshly
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the word that itself, cut short

explanation.surface: An exasperated complaint about a dreadful hotel that is just about solvent financially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reverses PAN to NAP. 'Solvent' looks financial but is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a volatile liquid hydrocarbon mixture used to dissolve other substances in industry.

clue.text: Billed one with some ingredients rising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, backwards
some means only part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A recipe is billed as containing some rising ingredients, like yeast.
explanation.definitionFit: An eider is a sea duck, and ducks are birds with bills, so it is a creature with a beak.

clue.text: Second half of Kama Sutra covers ground that's hot!

indicators.note: covers means one word is wrapped around the other
second half means drop the first two of the four letters, keeping the back two

explanation.surface: A cheeky joke that the back half of the Kama Sutra is the steamy bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large tropical Indonesian island, so it is land with a hot climate.

clue.text: Slipped disc, finally sent up on last pair of crutches

indicators.note: last pair of means keep only the final two letters of crutches

parts.note: the word crutches itself, all but its end removed

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of disc

parts.note: to send up is to mock, to ape someone

explanation.surface: Someone with a slipped disc ends up on their final pair of crutches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipped disc' looks like one phrase; 'Slipped' alone is the definition, meaning got away.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip away from captivity or a pursuer is to escape, so slipped is a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Ladder with its step shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a ladder's step is a rung

explanation.surface: A ladder whose step has been cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: The ladder is the one in tights or stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder in stockings is a vertical line of broken stitches, also called a run.

clue.text: Might one break clay when firing? Or has potter messed up?

definitions.text: Might one break clay when firing?

indicators.note: messed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pottery mishap: did the kiln break the clay, or did the potter botch it?
explanation.walkthrough: The clay is a clay pigeon and the firing is a gun, not a kiln.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapshooter fires at clay pigeons launched from a trap, aiming to shatter them.

clue.text: One planning romantic breaks with American husband

indicators.note: breaks means the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A romantic splits up with her American husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinator is a schemer who devises plots, so someone engaged in crafty planning.

clue.text: A lovely head showing wisdom

parts.note: cute means attractive, lovely
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place names

explanation.surface: A beautiful head that shows signs of intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Acuteness is sharpness of mind or perception, a quality close to shrewd judgment.

clue.text: See 2
Second leg: in the dressing rooms?

definitions.note: the answer is used as an adverb, meaning behind the scenes

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
a leg of a journey is a stage

explanation.surface: A footballer with a second leg injury is treated in the dressing rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage areas of a theatre, behind the scenes, are where performers have their dressing rooms.

clue.text: Creature mainly living from fir nuts collected by squirrel

indicators.note: collected by means held inside the other word

parts.note: to squirrel away is to stash

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A squirrel lives off nuts from a fir tree that it has gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly living' means living in the main, the sea, not living for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: A starfish is a marine echinoderm, an animal that lives in the sea, which poets call the main.

clue.text: Pulls in stomach muscles following end of liposuction

indicators.note: following means the muscles come after that letter
end of means take the last letter of liposuction

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles

explanation.surface: After liposuction, someone pulls in the stomach muscles to look trimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulls in' looks like holding the stomach in; it means arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab someone is to arrest them, the same as police pulling a suspect in.

clue.text: Stingy thing following sale, shelled out at the start: it might be in stock …

parts.note: a bee is a thing with a sting

indicators.note: shelled means the outer letters are removed
at the start means take the first letter of out

explanation.surface: Bargain hunters after a sale, wondering whether something is in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stingy' is not mean but 'having a sting'; 'stock' is livestock. The ellipsis links to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A beefalo is a cross between a domestic cow and a bison, raised as farm livestock.

clue.text: Second note put in score is wrong

indicators.note: wrong means the letters are in the wrong order, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician complains that a second note put into a score is incorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: In a major or minor scale, the supertonic is the degree immediately above the tonic, its second step.

clue.text: … it reminds you to buy new silver product

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
ware is a manufactured article, a product

explanation.surface: An advert prompts shoppers to buy a new silver gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues from the clue before via the ellipsis.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagware is software that keeps showing pop-ups urging the user to pay for the full licence.

clue.text: Private home page

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a page is one side of a sheet of paper

explanation.surface: A private web page, perhaps someone's personal home page.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside information is private, known only to those within a group, so inside works as confidential.

clue.text: Vegetable is raw, needing seasoning

parts.note: green means unripe or inexperienced, raw
pepper is a seasoning

explanation.surface: A raw vegetable needs some seasoning before it can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A green pepper is an unripe capsicum, eaten raw or cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Understanding of golf pars when going round

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters are turned about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer's grasp of scoring pars on a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A grasp of a subject is a firm comprehension of it, a synonym for knowing it well.

clue.text: Tartan Army's leader wearing top to support Portugal

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so Portugal comes first

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

indicators.note: wearing means the top is put on around the letter

parts.note: a lid is a top of a container

indicators.note: leader means take the first letter of Army's

explanation.surface: Scotland's Tartan Army football fans: their leader dons a shirt to cheer on Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tartan Army is the nickname for Scotland's football supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is twilled woollen cloth woven in a chequered tartan pattern.

clue.text: Hang back to talk

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way

parts.note: to sag is to hang down

explanation.surface: A shy person hangs back rather than chat.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is an informal verb meaning to chatter idly at length.

clue.text: Desire to be wealthy? Caviare is served

indicators.note: served suggests the letters are dished up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wanting to be rich: caviar is being served at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed, an excessive craving for money and riches.

clue.text: Character who discovered Treasure Island after a large cut, we hear

indicators.note: after means the island letter is placed behind the a-large pair
we hear means the word is said aloud and spelt by its sound

parts.note: a barber is one who cuts hair

explanation.surface: A treasure hunter in the Stevenson novel turns up after a big haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treasure Island' reads as the novel, but the definition stops at 'Treasure'. BABA is how 'barber' sounds in a non-rhotic British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, Ali Baba finds the robbers' hoard of riches in a cave.

clue.text: Food from scattered seeds: crop that might be corny?

indicators.note: scattered means the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: cheese, like cheesy, describes something corny and sentimental

explanation.surface: Food grown from scattered seeds, a crop that might be corn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corny' points at corn, but it means cheesy.
explanation.definitionFit: Processed cheese is a manufactured dairy product, an everyday foodstuff.
